The 2004 high-gelsemine treatment was explicitly set within the highest natural range. Starting cells were balanced at 20 plants per morph x treatment; reported deaths imply high n=38 and low n=37. Negative lnRR means fewer total pollinator visits on high-gelsemine plants. This natural-range year is the primary visitation effect for the study cluster.

Across 28 individually tested bees from five colonies, bees made 18% more visits to the highest-natural-range cardenolide flowers than sucrose controls; the Poisson GLMM reported Wald chi-square=2.15, df=1, p=0.14. The log contrast is reconstructed as ln(1.18), with SE inferred from the 1-df Wald statistic. Because the 18% contrast is rounded and raw/model coefficient data have not yet been recovered, this row is quantitative context but not pool-eligible. It is also distinct from the 10-day colony assay, where cardenolides became strongly deterrent over repeated exposure.
